lawyer:
Md Mahbub Ali-For the petitioner. 
Bishajit Roy, DAG with Swarup Kanti Deb, AAG-For the Respondent No. 5. 
M Khaled Ahmed, Advocate-For the Respondent No. 9.
parties:
Champa Deb ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Secretary, Ministry of Land and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Akram Hossain Chowdhury J : On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, this rule nisi was Issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as why the impugned order dated 9-5-2011 passed by the Land Appeal Board (Full Board), in Case No. 2-3/2010 (Full Board) Moulvibazar, dismissing the appeal and maintaining the order dated 24- 6-2003 passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura in Miscellaneous Case No. 16/ 2002-03, directing the Kanongoo and Upozilla Land Assistant Officer for correction of the record as Khas land in respect of the land of Plot No. 1569 of Khatian No. 366 measuring an area of 32 decimals, Plot No. 1569 of Khatian No. 369 measuring an area of 50 decimals, Plot No. 1049 of Khatian No. 382 measuring an area of 32 decimals, plot No. 1650 of Khatian No. 386 measuring an area of 36 decimals and Plot No. 1652 of Khatian No. 386 measuring an area of 60 decimals, in total 2.07 acres of land under JL No. 65/174, Mouza-Purba Monsurabad, Kulaura, District -Moulvibazar as contained in Annexure-L to the petition should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the respondent No. 7 should not directed to allow mutation in the name of the petitioner in respect of the aforesaid land and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may deem fit and proper, should not be passed.

2. The facts leading to the rule as averred in the writ petition, in brief, are that the petitioner was claiming that their ancestral land measuring 2.07 acres along with other lands were originally belonged to one Boishnav Chandra Deb who died leaving behind two sons namely, (1) Nagendra Chandra Deb and (2) Ganenra Chandra Deb; Ganendra Chandra was unmarried and died leaving behind his only brother Nagendra as his heir; Nagendra Chandra died leaving behind his son Champa Deb i.e. the present petitioner and one daughter Mira Rani as his heirs and thereby the petitioner owned the aforesaid land by way of inheritance. The petitioner used to possess the land in question but the SA Khatian Nos. 382, 386, 366 and 369 containing those property have been prepared in S.A. operation in the name of his father Nagendra Chandra Deb and his grandfather Boishnab Chandra Deb. However, since the petitioner being only son of his father Nagendra Chandra Deb and is possessing the land in question, as such, in the recent survey DP Khatian No. 1083 has been prepared in his name. After the death of his father, Nagendra Chandra Deb who was the SA recorded tenant, the petitioner filed Mutation Case being No.1730/2001-02 before the 'respondent No. 7, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura for mutating his name in separate khatian but in the meantime one Md. Mahmud Ali, the respondent No. 9 herein, with a view to grab the petitioner's ancestral property filed another Mutation Case being No 1327/2001-02 before the aforesaid respondent No. 7 under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (shortly SAT Act). Then both the mutation case were heard together by the respondent No.7, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura who after hearing by his order dated 10-11-2002 (Annexure-C) rejecting: both the mutation case directed the Tahsilder, respondent No. 8 to sent a proposal for declaring the land in question as government Khas land. In pursuant to that order of respondent No. 7 dated 10-11-2002 a Miscellaneous Case being No. 16/2002-03 was started for declaring the land in question as government khas land; in which behind the back of the petitioner, the respondent No. 9 collusively managed to have obtain a report dated 21-11-2003 stating that there is no heirs of the SA recorded owner Nagendra Chandra Deb in Bangladesh and thereby the respondent No. 7 vide his order dated 24-6-2003 (Annexure-D (1) directed the Kanongoo and Upazilla Land Assistant Officer (ULAO) to correct the khatian of record to the 90 Champa Deb vs Bangladesh (Md Akram Hossain Chowdhury .1) 21 BLC (2016) effect that the land in question is a government khas land. Thereafter, the petitioner against the order of the respondent No. 7 dated 10-11-2002 passed in Mutation Case No. 1730/2001-02, filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 5/2004 before the respondent No. 6, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Moulvibazar who after hearing the parties by his order dated 29-6-2004 (Annexure-E) sent the matter/case back on remand to the, respondent No. 7 to re-consider and dispose of the Mutation Case No. 1730/ 2001-02 after examining the documents and the identity placed by the petitioner. As per the remand order of respondent No. 6 dated 29-6- 2004 the respondent No. 7 again started a Miscellaneous Case being No. 2/2004-05 and after hearing vide his order dated 29-5-2005 (Annexure-F) rejecting the Misc. Case. No. 2/2004-05 uphold his earlier order passed on 10-11-2002. The petitioner challenging the said order of the respondent No. 7 dated 29-5-2005 again filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 3/2005 under section 147 of the SAT Act before the respondent No. 6, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Moulvibazar who after hearing the said appeal vide order dated 6-9-2005 (Annexure-G) dismissed the same with an observation that the, petitioner, if so desire, may sought his relief before the competent Civil Court.

3. By this time the respondent No. 9, Md. Mahmud Ali also filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 4/2005 before the respondent No.6 against the order of respondent No. 7 dated 24-6-2003 passed in miscellaneous Case. No. 16/2002-03 in order to correction of the record to the extent of the land in dispute as government khas land. After hearing the said appeal the respondent No. 6 dismissed the same with an observation that the respondent No. 9, Md Mahmud Ali may take legal recourse by filing an application before the Exchange Regularization Upazilla Committee (ERUC) or to file a civil suit in order to have the decision about his title through the alleged exchange deed. Accordingly, the respondent No. 9 though filed an application before the Exchange Regularization Upazilla Committee (ERUC) but no such deed of Exchange bearing No.7560 dated 9-12-1968 was submitted at the time of filing of .the mutation case before the respondent No. 7, as such the petitioner filed a written objection thereon.

4. In the meantime against the dismissal order of respondent No. 6 dated 6-9-2005 (Annexure-G) passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 3/2005 the petitioner filed a Revenue Miscellaneous Appeal being No. 109 of 2005 while the respondent No. 9 also filed a Revenue Miscellaneous Appeal No. 101 of 2005 before the Additional Divisional Commissioner (Rev.), Sylhet who after hearing both the appeals analogously vide his order dated 26-12-2006 (Annexure-I) dismissing the petitioner's appeal No. 109 of 2005 allowed the appeal No. 101 of 2005 of respondent No. 9 and stayed the order of respondent No. 7 dated 24-6-2003 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 16/2002-03 and also stayed the order of respondent No. 6 dated 6-9-2005 passed in Appeal No. 3/2005, till disposal of the application filed by the respondent No. 9 before the Exchange Regularization Upazilla Committee (ERUC).

5. Against the said order of the Additional Divisional Commissioner (Rev), Sylhet dated 26-12-2006 the petitioner filed Review Case No. 3 of 2007. Ultimately after hearing the said review case was allowed vide order dated 29-1-2008 (Annexure-J) and thereby the Additional Divisional Commissioner (Rev), Sylhet reviewing his own order dated 26-12-2006 set-aside the order allowing the appeal No. 101/2005 of the respondent No. 9 and directed the respondent No. 7 to mutate the petitioner's name in respect of the case land after correction of the Khatians.

6. Challenging the said review order of the Additional Divisional Commissioner (Rev), Sylhet dated 29-1-2008 the respondent No. 9 filed an Appeal being No. 2-23/2008 (Moulvibazar) before the Land Appeal Board, section-2, Dhaka in which the petitioner filed written statement and after hearing both the party a single member Board vide its order dated 4-1-2010 (Annexure-K) setting aside the order of the Additional Divisional Commissioner (Rev), Sylhet dated 29-1-2008 allowed the appeal of respondent No. 9, upholding the earlier order of the Additional Divisional Commissioner dated 26-12-2006 passed in Revenue Miscellaneous Appeal No. 101 of 2005.

7. Against that order of the Single Member Board dated 4-1-2010 the petitioner filed a case being No. 2-3/2010 (Full Board) Moulvibazar, before the full board of the Land Appeal Board, Dhaka and after hearing the said case the three member full board of the Land Appeal Board by the impugned order dated 9-5-2011 setting aside the order of the Single Member Board as well as the order, of the Additional Divisional Commissioner (Rev,), Sylhet dismissed the aforesaid case maintaining the order of respondent No. 7, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura dated 24-6-2003 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 16/2002-03 declaring the land in question as a government khas land having found the same as wasteland and abandoned.

8. Since the judgment and order of the Land Appeal Board is a final order under the statute, the petitioner having no other alternative efficacious remedy to redress his grievance, therefore, constrained to file the instant writ petition under Article 102 of the constitution and obtained the present rule.

9. It appears from the record that the present writ petition is a certiorari in nature, as because the legality and validity of the impugned Judgment and order was called in question; as such, the Lower Courts record requires to be examined but no LCR was called for at the time of issuance of the rule. However, the petitioner annexing the judgment and orders of the respective authority concerned obtained the present rule; and after that upon filing supplementary affidavits, other relating documents have also been filed by both the parties; hence, we find that so far as the judgments and other relating documents being filed, by this time, to this writ petition, as such, now it is convenient to this Court, without the Lower Court's record the present rule can be disposed of upon perusing and going through the annexures as annexed by both the party to this writ petition.

10. Mr Md Mahbub Ali, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner supporting the rule submits that the petitioner Champa Deb being a permanent resident of Bangladesh, residing near the land in question and has been possessing the same for a long time but the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura in deciding the mutation case under section 143 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act, disbelieved the petitioner's presence in Bangladesh though the petitioner presenting oral and documentary evidences has been able to prove his presence in Bangladesh as well as his possession in the property in dispute. He further submits that the respondent No. 7, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura without appreciating the legal proposition and non-maintaining the process as provided under section 92(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 but upon his own observations proceeded with the Miscellaneous Case No. 16/ 2002-03 for treating the land in dispute as government khas land. He also submits that the petitioner and his predecessors were all along in Bangladesh and never left the country any point of time; as such, declaring the land in dispute as government khas land is a malafide and arbitrary decision of the respondents, as such, the said decision of the respondents is liable to be declared as have been made without lawful authority. Mr. Ali further submits that the respondent No. 9 being mighty and powerful person in the locality who is trying to grab the petitioner's valuable property upon submitting an alleged exchange deed dated 09.12.1968 as to establish his title over the land m question which is legally barred under Article 300 of the Land Management Manual as to the validity of said exchange deed. Mr. Ali emphasis on his submissions to the extent that since the judgment and order of the Land Appeal Board is final, he has no other alternative efficacious remedy available against the impugned Judgment and order; as such, the petitioner has filed this writ petition in a certiorari manner to examine the legality and validity of the impugned Judgment by this Hon'ble Court under Article 102 of the constitution and there-by prays for making the rule absolute by declaring the impugned judgment and order as passed by the Land Appeal Board (Full Board) affirming the order of respondent No. 7 in order to declare the property in dispute as the government khas land is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

11. Mr M Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.9 by filing affidavit-in-oppositions and supplementary affidavits annexing therewith some annexures controverted some allegations of the petitioner and pointing out to the review order of the Additional Divisional Commissioner and thereby referring to a decision reported in 49 DLR (AD) 108 submits that a review was never meant and allowed to be utilized as another opportunity for rehearing the matter which is already closed by a final judgment. He also relying to a decision reported in 31 DLR (AD) 303 submits that there is a long line of decisions in favour of the view that the High court should not enter into disputed questions of fact nor decide any question as to title which require investigation into facts and taking of elaborate evidence. In support of his submission in opposing the rule Mr Khaled Ahmed further submits that the respondent No. 9, Md Mahbub An got an exchange deed from the predecessor of the petitioner long before of his entitlement of right in the property in question by Inheritance and the respondent No. 9 is possessing the land in dispute by paying rents to the government. The Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura as well as the Land Appeal Board (Full Board) without considering such aspects of this respondents case, disbelieved and affirmed the decision of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura in treating the property as government khas land; whereas, this respondent's has some establishment on the land in question and thereby he accrued the title and possession over the property by virtue of an exchange deed dated 9-12-1968.

12. Mr Bishajit Roy, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing with Mr. Swamp Kanti Deb, learned Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 5 by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contended that the respondent No. 7, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura upon complying all the process and formalities as provided under section 92 in as much as 92 (2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 initiated the Miscellaneous Case No, 16/2002-03 for treating the property as a government Khas land; because of that the property in question was being found abandoned and admittedly recorded as wasteland (পতিতভূমি) in the SA khatian. The property in dispute was being found ownerless and uncared of and therefore, the respondent No.7 upon hearing the objections of the parties under section 92 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act declared the property as government khas land. The learned DAG in support of his submission showing some khatians annexed to his affidavit in-opposition as annexure-2 series submits that the disputed property has already been shown in the recent published khatian as khas land and the Miscellaneous Case No. 16/2002-03 has been disposed of by correcting the records having there is no title of any persons other than the government of Bangladesh and showing that the property in question is a government khas land. He further submits that since the SA record was prepared showing the land as wasteland (পতিতভূমি) and abandoned, thereby the respondent No. 7, Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura rightly treated the property as government khas land. The Land Appeal Board being the last Court of facts in deciding the case under section 147 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 having found the process has been complied with legally and rightly, as such, affirming the order of the respondent No. 7, Assistant Commissioner (Land) Kulaura dismissed the appeal which deserves no interference.

13. Heard the learned Advocates of the respective parties, perused the writ petition, affidavit-in-oppositions, supplementary affidavits and the annexures annexed thereto. It appears that the Land Appeal Board (Full Board) in deciding the Case No. 2-3/2010 by its judgment and order dated 9-5-2011 held-

“উপযুক্ত পর্যালোচনার প্রেক্ষিতে দরখাস্তকারী এদেশের নাগরিক ও স্থায়ী বাসিন্দা মর্মে কোন দালিলিক প্রমাণ না থাকায় এবং প্রতিপক্ষের বিনিময় দলিল আইনত অকার্যকর হওয়ায় দরখাস্তকারী ও প্রতিপক্ষ কেইই এই মামলায় প্রতিকার পাওয়ার হকদার নহে।”

It also appears from the record that the present petitioner though filing a mutation case sought for mutating his name in separate khatian by claiming his title by way of Inheritance before the respondent No. 7 but he failed to prove his identity and presence in Bangladesh when the mutation case was taken up for hearing and also failed to prove as to the presence of S.A. recorded owners of the land in question i.e. the predecessors of the petitioner who were all along residing in this country. In appeal the respondent No. 6, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Moulvibazar initially upon hearing the appeal remanded the case to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) for rehearing the petitioner and also to examine his identity. Pursuant to that order of remand, though the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura heard the matter elaborately again and examined the documents supplied by the petitioner but found the petitioner's identity is questionable and upon holding an inquiry on the land in question found that the property was shown as wasteland (পতিতভূমি) as well as abandoned and also being uncared of Accordingly, the respondent No. 7 again decided the case holding that the land in question is being found ownerless and thereby upholding his earlier order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 16/2002-03 declared the property in question as government khas land. In appeal under section 147 while the matter was again taken up for hearing in review, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Moulvibazar found the title as appears from the pleadings of the respective parties are questionable and thereby dismissing the appeal has given a chance to the parties concerned to agitate their grievances before a competent Civil Court in deciding their title on the disputed land. However, the petitioner and respondent No.9 challenged the said decision of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Moulvibazar before the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet but the Additional Division Commissioner, Sylhet ultimately though passed a conflicting order, eventually at the end of the proceeding the full board of the Land Appeal Board finally uphold the decision of the respondent No. 7, Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura.

14. It reveals from the record that in deciding the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 5/2004 the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Moulvibazar in its order dated 29-6-2004 observed-

“ইতিপূর্বে ২২-৮-২০০২ তারিখে জনাব মোঃ মাহমুদ আলী তার নিকট শুধু একটি আমমোক্তার নামা আছে উল্লেখ করেছিলেন। কিন্তু বর্তমানে ভারতে রেজিষ্ট্রিকৃত একটি বিনিময় দলিলেরও তথ্য দিচ্ছেন । এক্ষেত্রে পূর্বের দেয়া তার বক্তব্যের সাথে বর্তমানে প্রদত্ত তথ্যের পূর্বাপর মিল বা সম্মতি নেই। তদুপরি তার কথিত দলিলটি ৯-১১-১৯৬৮ ইং তারিখে সম্পাদিত। উল্লেখ্য কেবলমাত্র ৬-৯-১৯৬৫ ইং তারিখের পূর্বে বিনিময়কৃত সম্পত্তিই নিয়মিত করার যোগ্য মর্মে ভূমি ব্যবস্থাপনা ম্যানুয়েলের ৩০০ অনুচ্ছেদে উল্লেখ আছে। যদিও এ বিষয়গুলো অত্র আপীল মামলায় বিবেচ্য নয় কিন্তু এক্ষেত্রে প্রাসঙ্গিক বিষয় অবশ্যেই প্রনিধান যোগ্য।” The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), the respondent. No. 6 further observed- “অতঃপর নালিশীভূমির রেকডীয় মালিক যেহেতু উক্ত সম্পত্তি ত্যাগ করে ভারতে চলে গেছেন এবং উক্ত সম্পত্তি ডিপি তালিকাভুক্ত হয়নি তাই উক্ত সম্পত্তি মালিকানাবিহীন সম্পত্তি হিসাবে গণ্য করে সহকারী কমিশনার (ভূমি), কুলাউড়া বিবিধ মোকদ্দমা নং ১৬/২০০২/২০০৩ এর মাধ্যমে সহকারী খাসভূমি হিসাবে রুপান্তরিত করে রেকর্ড সংশোধন করেন।”

15. For proper adjudication and disposal of the rule we may quote here the relevant sections 143, 147 and 150 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act 1950; which are as under:-

143. Maintenance of the record of rights-The Collector shall maintain up-to-date, in the prescribed manner, the record-of-rights prepared or revised under Part IV, (or under this part) by correcting clerical mistakes and by incorporating therein the changes on account of-

(a) The mutation of names as a result of transfer or inheritance;

(b) The subdivision, amalgamation or consolidation of holdings;

(c) The new settlement of lands or of holdings purchased by the Government and

(d) The abatement of rent on account of abandonment or diluvion or acquisition of land.

143A. Omitted.

143B. Correction of the Record-of-Rights upon inheritance-(1) Persons acquiring immovable property by inheritance according to their respective personal laws shall amicably effect partition of the property among them after the death of the propositus. After such partition, an instrument of partition shall be prepared and signed by all the concerned parties and shall be registered under the Registration Act, 1908.

(2) Upon presentation of the instrument of partition prepared, signed and registered under sub-section (1), the Revenue-officer shall revise the Khatian in accordance therewith.

143C. Procedure for Correction of the Record-of-Rights-(1) The Revenue officer on receipt of the notice under section 89 shall open a file for mutation of record-of-rights and shall issue notice to the co-sharers of the holding for mutation.

(2) For this purpose the Revenue-officer shall fix a date for objection if any. If no objection is raised within the stipulated period, the Revenue-officer shall correct the record-of-rights accordingly.

(3) If any objection is filed by any co-sharer of the holding, then the Revenue-officer shall fix a date for hearing both the parties, and after hearing, the Revenue-officer shall pass an order stating the reasons thereof, and the record-of-rights shall be corrected accordingly.

147. Appeals-Subject to any special provisions for appeal made in this part or in any rules made under this Act, an appeal shall lie from every original or appellate order made under any of the provisions of this part by a Revenue-officer as follows, namely: (a) To the Collector, when the order is made by a Revenue-officer subordinate to the Collector; (b) To the Commissioner of the division, when the order is made by the collector of a district within the division; and

(c) To the Board of Land Administration when the order is made by the Commissioner of a division.

150. Review by revenue-officer-(1) A Revenue-officer may, on application made in that behalf by any party interested or of his own motion, review any order passed by himself or by any of his predecessors in office under this part, and in so reviewing any order, may modify, reverse or confirm any such order:

Provided that-

(a) An application for review of an order shall not be entertained unless it is made within thirty days from the date of Such order or, when such application is presented after the expiry of the said period of thirty days, unless the applicant satisfies the Revenue-officer trial he had sufficient cause for not making the application within the said period;

(b) an order shall not be reviewed if an appeal has been preferred against such order or an application for revision of such order has been made to the superior Revenue authority; and

(c) an order shall not be modified or reversed on a review until reasonable notice has been given to the parties concerned to appear and be heard in the matter.

(2) No appeal shall lie from an order rejecting an application for review or confirming on a review any previous order.

We also may quote here section 92 of the SAT Act to refresh our memory how and in what procedure an interest of a raiyat can be extinguished. The section 92 is as follows:-

92. Extinguishment of Interest of Raiyats in Certain Cases-(1) The interest of a raiyat in a holding shall be extinguished-

(a) when he dies intestate leaving no heir entitled to inherit under the law of inheritance to which he is subject;

(b) when he surrenders- his holding at the end of any agricultural year by giving notice in the prescribed form and in the prescribed manner and within the prescribed period to the Revenue-officer;

(c) when he voluntarily abandons his  residence without making any  arrangement for payment of the  rent as it falls due and cases to cultivate his holding either by himself or by members of his family or by  or with the aid of servants or Jabourer with the aid of partners or bargadars for period of three successive years or-

(d) when such interest has devolved by inheritance, under the law of inheritance to which such raiyat is subject, on a person who is not a bond fide cultivator and such person has not cultivated the land comprised in the holding either by himself or by members of his family or by, or with the aid of, servants or laborers or with the aid of partners or bargadars during the period of five years from the date on which such interest has so devolved on him and there in no sufficient cause why he has not so cultivated the land.

(2) When the interest of a raiyat in a holding is extinguished under sub-section

(1), the Revenue-officer may enter on the holding; and the holding shall, with effect from the date on which the Revenue-officer so enters on it, vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances except the encumbrances on the holding which is extinguished under clause (a) of the said sub-section but the persons whose interests 'in the holdings are extinguished  under clauses (b) (c) and (d) of that sub-section shall continue to be personally liable for the money secured by the encumbrances on such holdings.

(3) Before entering on a holding under sub-section (2), the Revenue-officer shall cause a notice to be published in the prescribed manner declaring his intention to so enter on the holding and specifying the reasons thereof and also inviting objection from all persons interested in the holding and shall consider any objections that may be submitted to him within the period specified in that behalf in the notice and shall record a decision.

(4) Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Revenue-officer under sub-section (3) on any objection shown against the extinguishment of the interest of any raiyat in his holding under clause (d) of sub-section (1) may, instead of filing an appeal under section 147, institute a suit in the Civil Court against such order. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, such suit shall be filed within ninety days from the date of the order of the Revenue-officer under sub-section (3).

(5) All arrears of rent in respect of a holding remaining due from a raiyat whose interest in such holding has been extinguished under sub-section (1) shall be deemed to be irrecoverable.

<u>16. Upon going through and careful scrutiny of the above such provisions of law and the judgment and order passed by the Revenue Officer as well as the appellate authority under sections 143, 147 and 150 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 respectively, we find that Most of the authorities under this Act came to' a decision that the title of the suit property is very much questionable and from the SA record and the BS record the property in question appears to have been recorded as a wasteland (পতিতভূমি) As such the title of the disputed land could not be decided in a summary proceeding under sections 143 and 147 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. However, it also reveals from the record that the procedure under section 92 has been properly compiled with in extinguishing the interest of the original raiyat in treating the property as khas land and the petitioner and respondent No. 9 who claimed their respective title over the land having interest thereon challenged that decision by filing appeal under section 147 of the said Act.</u>

<u>17. In view of the above facts and circumstances we find reliance to a decision reported in 41 DLR 364 wherein Mr. Justice Mustafa Kamal, the then Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh, in deciding the case of Syed Ashfaque Hossain vs Government, of Bangladesh, in his Judgment at poragraph-25, referring to a unreported judgment of the Appellate Division passed in Civil Appeal No. 8 of 1972, the case of Bangladesh vs. Marium Khatun, categorically observed. "Section 143 of the Act is attracted only when a clerical mistake is to be corrected or, inter-alia, the mutation of names as result of transfer or inheritance is necessary. It is not attracted when the record-of-rights is to be corrected after a finding to be-given as to the title of the holders or the challengers. The examination of title deeds for purposes of determinating title of the holder of record of rights is not permitted under section 143.</u>

18. We also find reliance to a decision, the case of New Indian Tea. Company Ltd. vs Bangladesh reported in 31 DLR (AD) 303, where-in their Lordships in deciding the case categorically held, "There is a long line of decisions in favour of the view that the High Court should not enter into disputed questions of fact nor decide any question as to title which require investigation into facts and taking of elaborate evidence".

<u>19. So per so good, it is the settled principle of law that the disputed title cannot be decided in a summery proceedings under section 143 and 147 of the SAT Act or in a special Jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution other than by a competent Court of Civil Jurisdiction by taking elaborate evidence.</u>

20. Besides; the respondent No. 9 by virtue of an exchange deed dated 9-12-1968 though claimed his title in the disputed land but Article 300 of the Land Management Manual debarred the claimant for having such title by an exchange deed executed after the date of 6-9-1965. We do not find reliance to the decision reported in 49 DLR (AD) ,108, as referred by the learned Advocate for, the respondent No. 9; as because in the present case the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet reviewed its pwn order under section 150 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act, and the Land Appeal Board (Full Board) in their own jurisdiction decided in a separate case wherein the statute empowered the Revenue Officer and the Land Appeal Board '(Full Board) to reverse or modify its own order and of its subordinate authority but that has been done not under any other law other than under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.

21. Be that as it may, the petitioner though claimed his title by way of inheritance, but as such documents was properly placed or examined before a competent Court in support of his identity, in as much as of his title also but in a summery proceedings under section 143 of the SAT Act. It cannot I be decided; as because a Civil Court only can examine the documents to decide the title of a claimant. As per the proposition enunciated by our, apex Court in the cited decisions the disputed; question of facts and title could not be decided in a summary proceedings under section 143 or 147 of the State Acquisition &' Tenancy Act, 1950 or under Article 102 of the Constitution.

22. More so the petitioner and respondent No. 9 has appeared in the proceedings of Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 2002-03 as initiated under section 92 of the SAT Act to treat the property in dispute as government khas land and they also" challenged that order Of the Assistant Commissioner (Land); Kulaura by filing appeal provided under section 147' of the Act. As such, we are in a considered view that thy Miscellaneous Case. No. 16/2002-03 was initiated and contested properly by the petitioner and the respondent No. 9 who failed to prove their respective title in a proper forum to revise the decision of the authority concerned in deciding, the property is not government khas land. Hence, the petitioner may seek relief in a competent Civil Court to decide his title and possession over the land dispute by adducing elaborate oral and documentary evidences, if so he desire. As because as per. the proposition enunciated in the cited decisions and discussions made thereto, the disputed question of title and facts cannot be decided in a writ Jurisdiction.

23. In view of the matter and discussions made hereinabove we find no merit in the rule, thus, inclined to discharge the same.

In the result, the rule is discharged without, however, any order as to cost. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

Communicate the judgment and order at once.

End.
